title: Fugaro workspace credentials node
description: The node a workspace's owner publishes at `workspace_credentials/<name>` in the workspace's own database: the per-member table the workspace's service resolves a caller by, and the pool of credentials the workspace holds for its members' runs (docs/workspace-service/spec.md §4-§5). The workspace owner's CLI writes it and the workspace's own service reads it (WS4); a member's machine reads neither it nor the workspace's record, and no member's project can write it. It is version 2 of the node (R6, R7, U2): beside version 1's columns, a member's row says which concrete repositories each of its job accounts is a job of, and a pool entry says which kind of credential it is and, for a forge credential, which repositories it covers. Every object below the top level is closed (`additionalProperties: false`), because projectpolicy.DecodeWorkspaceCredentials reads a row strictly: a key an editor completed from this schema is a key the reader knows, and the other way round. The TOP LEVEL is the one exception and it is deliberate: an unknown key there is tolerated and listed (UnknownKeys), so a node a newer Fugaro wrote does not brick an older reader (P8).

version.description: The node's format version — this document describes version 2. The reader also reads version 1, the shape the release before this one wrote (a member's row with no job_account_repos, a pool entry with no kind, no all_members and no covers), because a workspace whose owner has not run `fugaro update` yet holds one; what version 1 does not say is not invented (an account carries no repository, and a pool entry is a model credential, which is the only kind the pool held, F15). Any other version is refused rather than read as the nearest one. Version 2 is published only after the service that reads it is deployed (WS4, R7), so a reader is never older than the writer.

name.description: The workspace's name: a Fugaro project name, and the last segment of the node's path `workspace_credentials/<name>`. It is the same grammar the workspace's record uses (F21) — a workspace name and a project name are written and read by the same flags — and it is the workspace owner's own project, not a member's.

members.description: The workspace's per-member table, in project-name order and each member once. This is the table the service resolves a caller by: it folds the email of a run's verified identity and looks the account up here, so one job account belongs to one row (Validate refuses an address two rows name, a caller whose member would depend on which row the lookup read first) and one Firebase project belongs to one row (the member's database is derived from it, so two rows naming one would read one member's policy, ledger and outcomes for both). A row with no job_account_repos at all is a member whose owner has not declared the repositories its accounts are jobs of — a version-1 row, or a member added before its repositories were written — and the service refuses that member's runs with the reason that names the owner's `fugaro update` (R19), never serves them.

shared.description: The credentials the workspace holds for its members' runs, in name order and each name once (D1298). **The credential's value is nowhere in this node** (rule 2 of spec.md §4): the node says which members may be served an entry, which kind of credential it is, and which repositories a forge entry reaches — the value itself lives in the workspace's own secret store and is never written to a database. An entry written with no projects at all is refused rather than read as "everybody" or as "nobody": offering a credential to every member is said with all_members.

repo.description: A concrete repository, in the one spelling this tree writes a repository in: `<provider>/<owner>/<name>` as projectpolicy.Canonical produces it (the provider segment first, ASCII lower-cased, no trailing `.git`, no `.` or `..` segment). A pattern is not one of these: `github/acme/*` and a bare `*` are refused where they are written (F42) — a pattern is a declaration about repositories that do not exist yet, checked against a member's live profile only when a run arrives, and this node's lists are the workspace owner's statement of the jobs and coverages they declared. What the member's own `allow_repos` list (which is a list of patterns) admits is asked separately, on the intersection (R5). The provider segment is a kind a repository's `git.provider` may be (internal/config's Providers); the schema names no enum of them, because that list is the one place the kinds exist (F15) and a second vocabulary here could disagree with it.
repo.$comment: projectpolicy.Canonical and the node's own reader hold a repository to this spelling; the pattern is the same grammar task.CanonicalRepo accepts, ASCII lower-cased.

job_account.description: One entry of a member row's job_account_repos: a job service account and the concrete repositories it is a job of (R6, D2992). The row's job_accounts and job_account_repos are ONE declaration written in one order — job_account_repos[i].account IS job_accounts[i] — which is why the repositories of an account cannot be read apart from the account: Validate refuses a row whose halves disagree (a different account at that position, a shorter or longer list of repositories), because a caller's repositories would then depend on which half the reader believed.

account.description: The job service account's address, exactly as the row's job_accounts carries it. It is the identity the workspace's service resolves a caller by (the `email` of the verified token, folded), so this is the account the repositories below are held to: a run presenting it is served only for a repository this list names.

repos.description: The concrete repositories this account is a job of, sorted and each once — one for a repository's own job, several for a shared project job (the workspaces design's O3 and O4, D2992). **An empty list is a state and not a mistake**: it says the account is a job of no repository this owner has declared, which is what a version-1 row decodes to and what a member whose repositories have not been declared yet carries; a run on such an account is refused by the service with the reason that names the owner's `fugaro update` (R19). A row that declares SOME of its accounts' repositories is neither state: it is a declaration whose reading would depend on which half a reader believed, and Validate refuses it.
repos.$comment: The list is held to this object's own grammar by the reader rather than by JSON Schema: sorted, no duplicates, and every entry a $defs/repo (projectpolicy.validateJobAccountRepos).

member.description: One member of the workspace: how the workspace's service reaches it, and nothing else. There is no `database_url` and no bucket here, and the row is closed so one cannot be added: the member's database is DERIVED from the Firebase project joined to the row's region (credsvc's workspaceDatabase), which is what makes two members' accounts unpointable at one database — the splice a database_url in a row would reopen (the post-merge review's finding 6). Writing the fields of one member's row beside another member's is the same attack by hand, which is why an unknown key inside a row is refused and not ignored.

project.description: The member's Fugaro project name: the namespace both this node and the workspace's record speak, and the name the shared pool's allow-lists use.

firebase_project.$comment: The same pattern as config.ProjectNameRE (internal/config/project.go), which the reader holds the Firebase project to.
firebase_project.description: The member's Firebase project id: the `aud` of a run identity minted there, and the half of the pair `aud`/`iss` that tells one member's tokens from another's. It is also the fact the member's database is derived from, so one Firebase project belongs to one member and Validate refuses a second row naming it.

database_region.description: The region the member's Realtime Database is in, or the empty string for a database in the project's default region — the two shapes the tree's own reader names a database with (internal/infra's CheckFirebaseOutputsFor): `<firebase_project>-default-rtdb.firebasedatabase.app` and the legacy `<firebase_project>-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com`. The project id still decides WHOSE database it is (the derivation the run identity's `iss` is held to); this field says only where in that project the database lives, and a row naming something that is not a region derives a host that is not a database.

fp.$comment: The same pattern as config.ProjectNameRE (internal/config/project.go), which the reader holds the fp to. That it is the SAME name as this row's project is Validate's rule and not expressible here.
fp.description: The member's Fugaro project name as the run identity's `fp` claim carries it. It is a field of its own rather than a second read of `project`, because the claim is what the check is made against and the two are compared: a row whose halves disagreed would admit one member's token as another member's run.

job_accounts.description: The member's job service accounts, by email, in the row's own order and each once across the whole node: the identities the service resolves a caller by. Version 2 adds the repositories beside this list as `job_account_repos` rather than retyping it — a field's meaning never changes (CLAUDE.md) — so this is the list of addresses a version-1 node carries, with exactly that meaning. At least one is required: a row naming none is a member the service can place nobody by, and two rows naming one account are a caller whose member depends on which row the lookup read first.

job_account_repos.description: The concrete repositories each of the row's job accounts is a job of: one entry per account of `job_accounts`, in that list's own order (R6, D2992). Written by the workspace owner, beside the accounts and not in their place. It is EMPTY — an empty list, or the key left out, which this reader reads the same — for a row that declares none, which is what a version-1 row is and what a member whose repositories have not been declared yet carries; nothing is invented for such a row, and the service refuses its runs (R19). A list that names some of the row's accounts is refused: a declaration read in halves is a caller whose repositories depend on which half the reader believed.
job_account_repos.$comment: The pairing with job_accounts is Validate's rule and not expressible here: JSON Schema cannot tie an array's entries to another array's entries in order.

exchange_url.description: The member's exchange endpoint, where the workspace's signer mints a member-bound assertion for (spec.md §3, D1293). It is `https` with a host and no query and no fragment, which is what the endpoint matches exactly; a URL that names no host, or carries a query, admits nobody. It is the owner's declaration of where the member is reached, and it is not a credential: nothing signs with it and no token is verified against it.

shared.description: One credential of the workspace's pool: what it is offered to, which kind it is, and — for a forge credential — which repositories it reaches. The credential's value is nowhere here (rule 2 of spec.md §4): the entry names it, and the name is what the member's own bundle and the cascade speak.
shared.$comment: all_members and projects are exclusive (R7) and one of them is written: an entry that names the members it is offered to carries projects and no all_members at all, and an entry offered to every member carries all_members and no projects. The writer omits them when they are empty rather than writing an empty list, so a reader cannot find a false beside a list and has to read the list. The reader also refuses an all_members written as false beside no projects (it offers the credential to nobody), which JSON Schema cannot say: a key that is present is present whatever it is set to.

name.description: The credential's name — the name the bundle's entry and the cascade both speak, and never a value. A pool entry's name is what the member's own policy's accounts block is asked about (MemberAdmitsShared), so a name two entries shared would be one credential whose value depends on which entry was read.

kind.description: Which kind of credential this entry is (U2, D2978, F15): the string `model`, or a kind a repository's `git.provider` may be (internal/config's Providers) for a forge credential. No enum is written here, because that list is where the kinds exist and a second vocabulary in this schema could disagree with it; the reader refuses a kind that is neither. The kind is also the first segment of every repository in `covers`, so a forge entry's kind and its coverage are one string and nothing maps one spelling onto another. It is what tells the service which route may serve the entry — a call is never routed to a credential of another kind.
kind.$comment: projectpolicy.SharedKindModel is the model kind; a forge kind is a member of config.Providers (internal/projectpolicy/workspace_credentials_v2.go's forgeKind).

all_members.description: Written `true` for a pool entry offered to every member of the workspace (R7, D2977) — and written at all only in that state: a `false` is refused by the reader rather than read as "the projects it names", because the two ways of saying who may be served an entry are this key and `projects`, and neither is the other's absence. The workspace owner's writer publishes it only for a workspace with a cap set and only after the cap meter is wired (D2977): the allow-list is the owner's fence over their own money, and without the meter nothing bounds a member who joins later. That rule is the writer's, because the node carries no cap and its own reader cannot ask it.

projects.description: The member projects this entry is offered to, sorted and each once: D1298's per-project allow-list, which is the workspace owner's fence over their own credential. An empty list written beside no `all_members` is refused rather than read as "everybody" or as "nobody" — a written shared credential that names no project is a half-written declaration, and the two readings of it are the one mistake that would either widen the pool to every member or hide the mistake behind a list that serves no one. The names are member projects of this workspace, and the service asks the member's own policy as well (D1298's intersection): an entry offered to a project is served only if that project also admits it.

covers.description: The concrete repositories a FORGE entry reaches, sorted and each once, whose provider segment is the entry's own `kind`: the workspace owner's list of the repositories their own credential is stored for (U2), which is the coverage the service holds a run to — never the member's list, and never a pattern (F42). A model entry carries none: the repositories a model call may be made for are the member's own policy's business, and an entry that named them would be a second, weaker answer to a question the member's policy already answers. Both mismatches are refused: a model entry that covers repositories, and a forge entry that covers none (an empty coverage is a half-written declaration).
covers.$comment: JSON Schema cannot say that every entry's first segment equals this object's kind, nor that the list is sorted and unique: projectpolicy.validateSharedEntryV2 holds both.
